finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test forwards the attacker-supplied req.body.callback URL to axios.post with no scheme, host, or private-range validation. The server can be made to POST {ping:true} to internal hosts or 169.254.169.254. Only the status code is returned, so the attack is blind. Severity MEDIUM. Redirects are followed by default.

trace.note: pub.post("/hooks/test") route, no auth middleware in this file
req.body.callback read and passed unchanged to axios.post
Only r.status returned to caller; response body discarded

finding.guards_checked: Scheme check: none. Host check: none (no URL parse, no allowlist). Auth: none in this file; public mount point not in repo, unverified. Private-range/metadata block: none. Redirect handling: axios default follows redirects, no maxRedirects:0.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19-21 has no scheme, host, or private-range check, no URL parse, and no maxRedirects setting. The only auth in the file is requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12), applied to the admin router, not pub. No file in the directory mounts pub, so no middleware is shown in front of it.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback unchanged to axios.post and routes.js:21 returns only r.status. No closing guard exists in routes.js:19-22. Whether the route is reachable without authentication depends on the mount point in the application entry point (not in this directory), so the attacker-control premise cannot be confirmed here; if pub is mounted without auth middleware, the finding is CONFIRMED.

finding.claim: Admin-gated GET /diagnostics/fetch forwards req.query.url to axios.get with no scheme, host, or private-range validation. An admin session holder can reach internal hosts and metadata endpoints. Only the status code is returned. Severity MEDIUM because the attacker needs an admin session, and that precondition does not close SSRF to internal targets. Redirects are followed by default.

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applies to all admin routes
req.query.url read and passed unchanged to axios.get
Only r.status returned to caller; response body discarded

finding.guards_checked: Auth: requireAdmin enforces session role admin. Scheme check: none. Host check: none. Private-range/metadata block: none. Redirect handling: axios default follows redirects.

verdict.guard_found: none. No scheme, host, or private-range check exists. The only gate is requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied via admin.use at routes.js:12), which checks session role, not the URL.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches routes.js (8, 12, 14, 15, 16), and no closing URL guard exists at routes.js:15. The source fails the rubric's attacker-control test: req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only after requireAdmin (routes.js:8) passes, so the attacker must already hold an admin session, which is neither unauthenticated nor low-privilege. The SSRF is real but the finding's threat model does not meet the stated CONFIRMED bar. Note for re-scoping: a cross-site request that makes an admin's browser hit this GET could bring the source within reach of a low-privilege attacker, but that depends on session-cookie and SameSite settings that are not in this directory.
